gaps.sentence: 'I'll finish the report today,' she said. She said she would finish the report ___.
gaps.explanation: Today becomes that day when reported later.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: The hijackers ___ to blow up the plane unless their demands were met.
gaps.explanation: A declared harmful action is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
gaps.explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'How long have you worked here?' she asked him. She asked him how long he ___ there.
gaps.explanation: have worked → had worked; 'here' becomes 'there' in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.
